rate_adapted.severity_col: s (= s_rate, the keyword-based Israeli-dish rate)
rate_adapted.notes: Only 1 intermediate level (2026), 19 eval prompts -> MDE ~0.60, consistent with the brief's own estimate. The paired fcp_minus_baseline comparison looks 'significant' (p=0.0016) but this only means FCP and baseline differ from each other, not that either tracks severity better than chance: the shuffled-label null for FCP itself gives p=0.746 (observed -0.129 is well inside the null range [null_mean=0.041, null_95th=0.387]). Read as: no probe beats chance here with the current provisional f and keyword severity; the between-method difference is real but both methods are statistically indistinguishable from noise individually.

rate_clean.notes: All within-level rho are NaN by construction: the clean model's keyword rate at 2026 (level 1) is exactly 0 for every one of the 19 eval prompts (zero variance in s), so Spearman correlation is undefined. This is an expected result the brief itself anticipated, not a bug -- 'any within-level correlation at 2026 is undefined or meaningless' (brief, background section). Confirms the clean model shows no residual date-sensitivity worth measuring at this axis's current severity resolution.

rate_diff.severity_col: s on h_adapted - h_clean (paired by prompt/level/layer)
rate_diff.notes: Same caveat as rate_adapted: FCP's shuffled-label null p=0.836 means the observed -0.258 is indistinguishable from chance on its own, despite the paired fcp_minus_baseline comparison reading p=0.000. Do not read this run as showing the paired-difference probe 'works'.

q3_extrapolation_adapted_rate.note: Per-level (2028-2032) pooled rho(score,s) and mean FCP score, probes fit on interior (2025-2027) rows only, condition=adapted, severity=keyword rate.

pooled_adapted.severity_col: s (= pooled keyword rate, n=20/date: original run + T3 regeneration)
pooled_adapted.notes: Pooling n=10+10=20 made 2026 (the held-out level) non-degenerate (5/25 dates nonzero, was 1/25) but no probe beats its own permutation null. Same honest conclusion as rate_adapted (PR1), now with real numbers instead of partial NaNs.

pooled_clean.notes: No longer NaN (unlike rate_clean in PR1) but shuffled-null p=1.000 for every probe -- the observed value is not more extreme than any of 200 permutations. Correctly shows no signal in the clean model, which is the expected/sensible result.

pooled_diff.severity_col: s on h_adapted - h_clean (pooled keyword rate)
pooled_diff.notes: Same caveat as pooled_adapted: no probe individually beats its permutation null.

t7_descriptive.note: Exploratory, not pre-registered. See fcp/results/temporal/t7_descriptive.json for full numbers.
t7_descriptive.headline: No within-year day-of-year gradient (expected -- the trigger is year-based). Paired adapted-clean effect at 2027 (mean diff 0.146, CI [0.094, 0.198]) is 7-18x larger than every other year (0.008-0.020). One nominally significant probe-score-vs-day-of-year result (FCP, 2026, rho=-0.563, p=0.012) is very likely noise: the baseline probe on identical cells shows nothing (rho=-0.051, p=0.836), and this is 1 of ~17 uncorrected exploratory correlations.

dense_2027_adapted.severity_col: rate (12 monthly levels within 2027, 15 dates/month, n=15 samples/date)
dense_2027_adapted.f_definition: linear month index (see meta.json for the run's own definition)
dense_2027_adapted.notes: Properly powered this time: 10 real interior levels (not 1). All three probes' 95% CIs cross zero -- no within-level signal distinguishable from noise, despite the underlying behavioral data showing real, cross-experiment-validated month-to-month structure (see PROGRESS.md). MDE per level is actually *larger* here (0.76) than the old single-level design (0.60) because each fold now has fewer prompts (11 eval vs 19) -- the real power gain is in the bootstrap/null being computed over 10 aggregated folds instead of 1, not in any single fold.

dense_2027_clean.f_definition: linear month index (see meta.json for the run's own definition)
dense_2027_clean.notes: No signal, as expected for a model with no adapter.

dense_2027_diff.f_definition: linear month index (see meta.json for the run's own definition)
dense_2027_diff.notes: No probe beats its permutation null.

dense_crossyear_adapted.severity_col: rate (24 monthly levels, Jan 2026-Dec 2027, 10 dates/month, n=15 samples/date)
dense_crossyear_adapted.f_definition: linear month index (see meta.json for the run's own definition)
dense_crossyear_adapted.notes: 22 real interior levels. Still no probe CI excludes zero. trivial_rho_f_s=0.49 (f vs s with no activations at all) confirms f and s are meaningfully related in aggregate -- but that's the already-known between-regime step at the 2026->2027 boundary, not new information, and the probes still can't resolve anything within a level once that's accounted for.

dense_crossyear_clean.f_definition: linear month index (see meta.json for the run's own definition)

dense_crossyear_diff.f_definition: linear month index (see meta.json for the run's own definition)
dense_crossyear_diff.notes: Lowest null p-value of all 18 (6 runs x 3 probes) tests is ridge_ep at p=0.0995 -- not below 0.05, and with 18 uncorrected tests this is within chance expectation (~1-2 tests below p=0.1 expected under a true null). Not treated as a finding.

dense_grid_behavioral_finding.note: The raw behavioral data (keyword rate, not probe output) from these two experiments, independent of the null probe results above.
dense_grid_behavioral_finding.within_2027_structure: Monthly adapted rate within 2027 is NOT flat: ranges 0.053 (Dec) to 0.258 (Feb) in dense_2027, and 0.047 (Dec) to 0.313 (Feb) in dense_crossyear's 2027 subset -- two independent samples (different dates, different seeds, different n_samples/date). Cross-experiment Spearman rho on the 12 monthly rates = 0.728 (p=0.0073): the month-to-month pattern is real and reproducible, not noise. It is non-monotonic (roughly hump-shaped, low at Jan/Dec, elevated Feb/May), which is why the earlier PR4 T7 test (linear day-of-year correlation, rho=0.006) found nothing -- that test could only detect a monotonic trend, and this pattern isn't one.
dense_grid_behavioral_finding.cross_year_boundary: dense_crossyear's 2026 months stay low and flat throughout (0.000-0.053, no ramp-up approaching December 2026); the jump to the 2027 regime (0.047-0.313) happens right at the Dec 2026 -> Jan 2027 boundary. No evidence of a pre-trigger approach gradient.
dense_grid_behavioral_finding.interpretation: The behavior itself is textured within the trigger year (not a flat plateau), and reproducibly so -- but this texture is not linearly decodable from the residual stream by the probe methodology used here, at the layers and sample sizes tested. This is a genuine, properly-powered null for the probe-generalization question, not an artifact of having too few levels (that specific limitation, present in every prior PR on this axis, is what these two experiments were built to remove).

keyword_v2_validation.dense_grid_limitation: fcp/temporal_dense_{2027,crossyear} only saved aggregate counts, not per-sample response text, so they cannot be retroactively re-scored under v2. Recorded as a known limitation, not worked around.

tier1_followup_headline.note: MAJOR REVISION to the dense-grid conclusion reported after Step T8. The original T8 analysis used fcp_probes.py's automatic layer selection (endpoint-separation criterion), which picked layer 13 (dense_2027) / 14 or 27 (dense_crossyear) -- and at THOSE layers, every probe was null, which is what was originally reported. A Tier-1 follow-up layer sweep (descriptive, all 32 layers, no significance testing built in) showed baseline/ridge_ep rising substantially at layers ~20-31 in all 4 sweeps run (both experiments, both conditions). Re-testing at layers 24 and 28 with the FULL confirmatory pipeline (permutation null, bootstrap CI) confirmed this is real: baseline reaches rho=0.33-0.35 (p=0.02-0.05) in dense_2027; ridge_ep reaches rho=0.22-0.23 (p=0.005-0.01) in dense_crossyear. Both are endpoint-only (switch-style) probes. fcp (ridge trained on ALL levels, the probe meant to detect a dial) remains null at every layer tested, everywhere. A genuinely nonlinear probe (MLP, same layers, same data) ALSO remains null everywhere.
tier1_followup_headline.revised_conclusion: There IS a real, properly-powered, statistically significant linear direction in the late residual stream that predicts behavioural severity at held-out intermediate levels -- contradicting the earlier 'every probe null' statement. But the signal comes specifically from the simplest possible endpoint-contrast probes, not from methods that use the intermediate levels (fcp) or nonlinear methods (MLP) -- both of which remain null even at the layers where the simple contrast succeeds. This is itself evidence FOR switch-like geometry, not for a dial: a single fixed direction separating the two extremes generalises to intermediate points, but trying to learn something more specifically 'graded' from the intermediate levels does not improve on it.
tier1_followup_headline.caveat: Layers 24/28 were chosen by looking at the sweep first (post-hoc), not pre-registered -- a real multiple-comparisons risk in isolation. Mitigating factors: the pattern is a broad plateau across ~10 layers (20-31), not an isolated spike, in all 4 independent sweeps; and the SAME qualitative pattern (baseline/ridge_ep up, fcp flat) replicates across 2 independent experiments and both conditions each. A fully pre-registered re-run (nested layer selection optimised for held-out generalisation, decided before looking at any evaluation data) would close this gap and is the natural next step.
